title: Evaluating RAG: measuring retrieval, not just the final answer
hook: A good final answer can hide bad retrieval, and a good retrieval can hide a bad final answer; measure both separately.
inPlainWords: To know whether a RAG system is actually working, measure how often search finds the right passage, and separately, how often the model's answer is faithful to what it found.

useCase.title: The bot 'seems fine' but nobody has measured it
useCase.story: The support assistant has been live for two months. The team gets occasional complaints but no real numbers: how often does search find the right passage, how often does the model use it correctly, and how would they know if a change made things better or worse?

approaches.name: Judge only the final answer by eye
approaches.what: Read the customer-facing text and decide if it looks right.
approaches.greatWhen: As a first, rough smoke test on a handful of examples.
approaches.avoidWhen: Used as the only method at scale, since it hides whether the failure is retrieval or generation and doesn't scale to hundreds of changes.
approaches.example: A reviewer skims 10 answers and calls it "fine."

approaches.name: Measure retrieval separately, with a labeled set
approaches.what: Build a set of questions with the known-correct passage for each, then measure how often and how high that passage is retrieved.
approaches.greatWhen: You want to isolate retrieval problems from generation problems.
approaches.avoidWhen: No team member is available to label the correct passages at first.
approaches.example: 91% of 50 labeled questions retrieve the right passage in the top 3.

approaches.name: Measure faithfulness: did the answer only use what was retrieved
approaches.what: Check whether the final answer's claims are supported by the retrieved passages.
approaches.greatWhen: Retrieval already looks fine but answers are still sometimes wrong.
approaches.avoidWhen: Skipped before retrieval quality is confirmed, since errors get misattributed.
approaches.example: 96% of answers are fully supported by what was retrieved.

approaches.name: Run a golden question set before every change
approaches.what: A fixed set of representative questions with known-good answers, re-run automatically whenever the pipeline changes.
approaches.avoidWhen: Never skip; without it, fixes silently break other questions.
approaches.example: Every pull request re-runs the same 50 questions and reports any score that drops.

approaches.name: Sample real traffic for ongoing feedback
approaches.what: Periodically review a sample of live conversations for accuracy, not just the golden set.
approaches.greatWhen: Golden sets go stale and miss real, evolving customer phrasing.
approaches.avoidWhen: Relying on it alone instead of a golden set, since sampling is slower to catch regressions.
approaches.example: A weekly review of 100 real conversations surfaces a new phrasing the golden set never covered.

challenge.question: The team wants to know whether a chunking change improved or hurt the assistant. What should they measure?

options.text: Retrieval accuracy against a labeled question set, faithfulness of answers to retrieved passages, and results on a golden question set before and after the change
options.why: Separates retrieval quality from generation quality and catches regressions automatically.

options.text: Read 10 new answers and see if they look right
options.why: Too small a sample, and doesn't separate the cause of any problem found.

options.text: Only measure how fast responses come back
options.why: Speed says nothing about whether answers are correct.

options.text: Wait for customer complaints to tell you
options.why: Real signal eventually, but slow, incomplete and reactive rather than catching regressions before launch.

bestCase.title: Numbers before and after every change
bestCase.example: Before changing chunk size, the team runs the golden set: 91% retrieval accuracy, 96% faithfulness. After the change: 95% and 97%. The change ships with evidence, not a guess.

worstCase.title: Shipping on vibes
worstCase.example: The team changes the prompt because a few answers looked odd. Retrieval accuracy quietly drops from 91% to 78% because nobody was measuring it, and complaints rise for a month before anyone notices.

route.travelling: A proposed change to chunk size

steps.label: Build a labeled question set
steps.goes: 50 real questions, each with the correct passage marked.

steps.label: Measure retrieval accuracy
steps.goes: 91% of questions retrieve the correct passage in the top 3.

steps.label: Measure faithfulness
steps.goes: 96% of answers are fully supported by what was retrieved.

steps.label: Make the change
steps.goes: Chunk size is adjusted to keep tables intact.

steps.label: Re-run the same measurements
steps.goesWrong: The team skips re-measuring and ships based on a few answers looking fine.

steps.label: Ship with evidence
steps.goes: The change goes live with before-and-after numbers on record.

takeaway: Measure retrieval accuracy and answer faithfulness separately, on a fixed question set, before and after every change; don't judge RAG by reading a few answers.
